subject: Dedicated throughput bands & measurement proposal
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@fintechco.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated — initial throughput ask

Rachel — thanks for the call this morning. A few quick clarifications so our procurement and infra teams can size the budget:

1) We need committed throughput guarantees in two dimensions: tokens/sec (for batching pricing) and requests/sec (for concurrency-sensitive endpoints).
2) Latency SLOs matter to us: p95 text-gen latency target of <= 350ms for short prompts (~128 tokens) and p99 <= 900ms.

Can you share a concise measurement methodology so we can validate an acceptance run prior to committing? Also, we expect a table of commit tiers and associated discounts for a 12‑month reserved capacity.

Thanks —
Alex
Platform Eng, FinTech Co

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — initial throughput ask

Alex — great to sync. FWIW attaching a short proposal that covers: throughput bands, recommended GPU pool sizes per band, proposed latency targets, and a reproducible measurement plan. Quick highlights below and the plan is attached as PDF + a small harness README: redwood_throughput_bands_v1.pdf, measurement_harness_instructions.md.

Summary bullets:
- Throughput bands: Bronze (up to 100k tokens/sec), Silver (100k–400k), Gold (400k–1.2M). We size GPU pools by steady-state concurrent requests and average tokens per request.
- Metrics: commit guarantees will be expressed as tokens/sec (sustained 15‑minute window) and requests/sec (sustained 1‑minute window). We include warm-cache and cold-cache runs separately.
- Latency: p95/p99 targets are set per model/sequence class; for your short prompts we propose p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 850ms on Gold band, slightly looser on Silver/Bronze.
- Measurement methodology: we provide a harness that drives a mix of prompt lengths, instruments token-emit timestamps, and reproduces the customer's real-world request distribution. Acceptance run is ~3 hours including cache priming.

Ben/Marissa — please review pricing bands in the attached XLS and propose the 12-month discount for FT-2026-0421.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — initial throughput ask

Looping in pricing & infra notes. Key points to decide before we finalize an offer:

- Measurement windows: Alex asked for tokens/sec and requests/sec. We should make the tokens/sec window 15 minutes as Rachel suggested and request/sec 1 minute to capture bursts. Would like to add a allowed performance degradation band: up to 5% under target before crediting.
- Warm vs cold cache: acceptance runs should include an explicit cache-priming phase (30–45 minutes) and then steady-state. We must record warm-cache hit-rates and KV cache priming steps (we'll share script).
- GPU pool sizing: propose mapping table in XLS: e.g., Gold => 16x A100 equivalent, Silver => 8x, Bronze => 4x. We will include headroom factor (1.2x) for safety.
- Discounts: for a 12‑month reserved commit we can propose: Bronze 18% off list, Silver 26%, Gold 35%, with a 5% additional credit for multi-year or early payment.

Aditya — can you confirm if our current dedicated runtime supports the p99 measurement instrumentation we need (per-token timestamps + per-request tracing)?

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — initial throughput ask

Ben/Rachel — yes, runtime supports the required telemetry. A few implementation notes for the measurement plan:

- Per-token emit times are logged at the serving edge. We can export an artifact with token timestamps and request IDs for the acceptance run.
- For requests/sec burst capture we suggest running two modes: steady (Poisson arrival matching your production traces) and stress bursts (10x short bursts for 60s) to validate autoscaling and headroom.
- Latency targets should be measured after the KV cache has been primed. We’ll run baseline cold-cache run for comparison but acceptance is judged on warm-cache results.
- We recommend defining sequence classes (SHORT: <=128 tokens, MEDIUM: 128–512, LONG: >512) and reporting p50/p95/p99 per class.

I’ll attach the harness README to the drive link. We should also record CPU/GPU utilization and queue lengths during the run and include that in the acceptance report.

— Aditya
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@fintechco.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — initial throughput ask

Thanks all — this is very helpful. A few follow-ups and asks from procurement before we proceed: 

1) Can you commit to an SLA credit table tied to tokens/sec shortfall and p99 misses? Procurement wants clear dollar credits per percentage-point deviation for the Gold band.
2) Please confirm the acceptance test timing: a single 3‑hour run (45m warm, 2h steady, 15m wrap) or multiple runs over different days? We prefer a single continuous run.
3) For pricing, can you convert the XLS bands into a single-line proposal with committed tokens/sec, requests/sec, expected GPU pool size, monthly committed spend, and effective discount? That will make approvals faster.

If you can get these edits back by Wednesday EOD, we can fast-track.

Alex

On Thu, Jul 22, 2026 at 09:35 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — noted. We'll produce a single-line commitment table and an SLA credit appendix tied to shortfall buckets.
> 
> I'll coordinate with Ben and Aditya to finalize the harness schedule — we can support a single continuous 3‑hour acceptance run; we'll capture warm-cache metrics during the run and provide the artifact.
> 
> Sending updated proposal by Wed EOD.
> 
> Rachel
